title: حِكَايَةُ التَّاجِرِ وَأَوْلَادِهِ
titleEn: The Merchant and His Sons, continued
part: Night 43 · The Merchant and His Sons, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 344–347 (Night 43, continuing directly from nights-42), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 43 follows Qūt al-Qulūb, who after eighty days in the dark chamber is overheard by the Caliph reciting verses in praise of Ghānim; she wins leave to search for him, gives alms in the markets, and is led to a sick stranger lying in a market-chief's house without recognising him. The chief then brings her a mother and daughter in sackcloth, who prove to be Ghānim's own mother and sister. Shahrazād is overtaken by morning. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الثَّالِثَةُ وَالْأَرْبَعُونَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-thālithatu wa-al-arbaʿūna
sentences.l: And-when came-to-be the-night, the-third-one and-the-forty,
sentences.i: When the forty-third night came,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا لْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُأَنَّ قُوتَ الْقُلُوبِ لَمَّا غَضِبَ عَلَيْهَا الْخَلِيفَةُ وَأَسْكَنَهَا فِى الْمَكَانِ الْمُظْلِمِ وَتَمَّتْ عَلَى هَذَا الْحَالِ ثَمَانِينَ يَوْمًا
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna Qūta al-Qulūbi lammā ghaḍiba ʿalayhā al-khalīfatu wa-askanahā fī al-makāni al-muẓlimi wa-tammat ʿalā hādhā al-ḥāli thamānīna yawman
sentences.l: She-said: It-has-reached-me, O the-king the-fortunate-that Qūt al-Qulūb, when became-angry at-her the-caliph and-lodged-her in the-place the-dark, and-continued upon this the-state eighty day-(acc.).
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that when the Caliph grew angry with Qūt al-Qulūb and lodged her in the dark place, she remained in that condition for eighty days.
sentences.n: The print gives لملك for الملك (the alif is dropped), read al-malik; we point the word as printed, لْمَلِكُ. It also runs السعيد and أن together into one word, السعيدان; we keep the printed letters but read saʿīdu anna. Likewise فى is printed with a dotless ى, read fī.

sentences.t: فَاتَّفَقَ أَنَّ الْخَلِيفَةَ مَرَّ يَوْمًا مِنَ الْأَيَّامِ عَلَى ذَلِكَ الْمَكَانِ فَسَمِعَ قُوتَ الْقُلُوبِ تُنْشِدُ الْأَشْعَارَ
sentences.tr: fa-ittafaqa anna al-khalīfata marra yawman mina al-ayyāmi ʿalā dhālika al-makāni fa-samiʿa Qūta al-Qulūbi tunshidu al-ashʿāra
sentences.l: And-it-chanced that the-caliph passed a-day from the-days by that the-place, and-heard Qūt al-Qulūb reciting the-verses.
sentences.i: It chanced that the Caliph passed that place one day, and he heard Qūt al-Qulūb reciting verses.
sentences.n: مرّ على is the verb of passing by a place; مِنَ الْأَيَّامِ ('one of the days') is the usual idiom for 'one day'.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَتْ مِنْ شِعْرِهَا قَالَتْ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faraghat min shiʿrihā qālat
sentences.l: And-when she-finished from her-poetry, she-said:
sentences.i: When she had finished her poetry, she said:

sentences.t: يَا حَبِيبِي يَا غَانِمُ مَا أَحْسَنَكَ وَمَا أَعَفَّ نَفْسَكَ
sentences.tr: yā ḥabībī yā Ghānimu mā aḥsanaka wa-mā aʿaffa nafsaka
sentences.l: O my-beloved, O Ghānim, how-good you, and-how-chaste your-self!
sentences.i: O my beloved Ghānim, how good you are, and how chaste of soul!
sentences.n: ما أحسنك and ما أعفّ are the exclamatory pattern mā afʿala, 'how very ...!'; the object that follows (-ka, nafsaka) is accusative.

sentences.t: أَحْسَنْتَ لِمَنْ أَسَاءَ عَلَيْكَ وَحَفِظْتَ حُرْمَةَ مَنْ ضَيَّعَ حُرْمَتَكَ وَحَفِظْتَ حَرِيمَهُ
sentences.tr: aḥsanta li-man asāʾa ʿalayka wa-ḥafiẓta ḥurmata man ḍayyaʿa ḥurmataka wa-ḥafiẓta ḥarīmahu
sentences.l: You-did-good to-whoever did-ill against-you, and-you-guarded the-sanctity-of whoever squandered your-sanctity, and-you-guarded his-women-folk.
sentences.i: You did good to him who did you ill, and you guarded the honour of one who squandered your honour, and you guarded his women.
sentences.n: حريمه (ḥarīm) is the women of a household, its inviolable precinct; here it is the Caliph's harem, which Ghānim spared. Qūt al-Qulūb means that Ghānim saw her and did not touch her.

sentences.t: وَهُوَ سَبَاكَ وَسَبَى أَهْلَكَ
sentences.tr: wa-huwa sabāka wa-sabā ahlaka
sentences.l: And-he took-you-captive and-took-captive your-family.
sentences.i: And he it was who took you captive, and took your family captive.
sentences.n: سبى (sabā) is to take captive, to carry off as a prisoner; the print writes the final ى with no dots in both verbs.

sentences.t: وَلَابُدَّ أَنْ تَقِفَ أَنْتَ وَأَمِيرَالْمُؤْمِنِينَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْ حَاكِمٍ عَادِلٍ وَتَنْتَصِفَ أَنْتَ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-lā budda an taqifa anta wa-amīra al-muʾminīna bayna yaday ḥākimin ʿādilin wa-tantaṣifa anta ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And-no escape that you-stand, you and-commander-of the-believers, between the-two-hands-of a-judge, a-just-one, and-you-get-justice, you, against-him.
sentences.i: And surely you and the Commander of the Faithful must stand before a just judge, and you shall obtain justice against him,
sentences.n: أميرالمؤمنين is printed as one word, amīr al-muʾminīn, and we keep it so. لابدّ ان is 'it cannot be otherwise than that'; بين يدي, literally 'between the two hands of', means 'in the presence of'. انتصف من / على is to take one's due, to get redress.

sentences.t: فِي يَوْمٍ يَكُونُ فِيهِ الْقَاضِي الْمَوْلَى جَلَّ وَعَزَّ وَالشُّهُو دْهُمُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ
sentences.tr: fī yawmin yakūnu fīhi al-qāḍī al-mawlā jalla wa-ʿazza wa-al-shuhū dhum al-malāʾikatu
sentences.l: On a-day there-is in-it the-judge the-Lord, may-He-be-majestic and-mighty, and-the-witnesses, they, the-angels.
sentences.i: on a day when the Judge shall be the Lord, glorious and mighty, and the witnesses shall be the angels.
sentences.n: The print splits والشهود هم oddly, as والشهو and دهم, with the dāl detached from its word; we keep the printed division but read wa-al-shuhūd hum, 'and the witnesses, they ...'. جل وعز is the pious formula 'exalted and mighty be He'.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْخَلِيفَةُ كَلَامَهَا وَفَهِمَ شَكْوَاهَا عَلِمَ أَنَّهَا مَظْلُومَةٌ فَدَخَلَ قَصْرَهُ وَأَرْسَلَ مَسْرُورَ الْخَادِمَ لَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-khalīfatu kalāmahā wa-fahima shakwāhā ʿalima annahā maẓlūmatun fa-dakhala qaṣrahu wa-arsala Masrūra al-khādima lahā
sentences.l: And-when heard the-caliph her-speech and-understood her-complaint, he-knew that-she a-wronged-one, and-entered his-palace and-sent Masrūr the-servant for-her.
sentences.i: When the Caliph had heard her words and understood her complaint, he knew that she had been wronged; so he went into his palace and sent Masrūr the eunuch to fetch her.
sentences.n: مسرور الخادم is printed without the accusative alif (مسرورًا); read it as the object of أرسل. لها, 'to her', here means 'for her', 'to bring her'. الخادم, 'the servant', is the usual word for the palace eunuch.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا حَضَرَتْ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ أَطْرَقَتْ بِرَأْسِهَا وَهِيَ بَاكِيَةُ الْعَيْنِ حَزِينَةُ الْقَلْبِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ḥaḍarat bayna yadayhi aṭraqat bi-raʾsihā wa-hiya bākiyatu al-ʿayni ḥazīnatu al-qalbi
sentences.l: And-when she-attended between his-two-hands, she-bowed-down with-her-head, and-she weeping-of the-eye, grieving-of the-heart.
sentences.i: When she came into his presence she bowed her head, weeping-eyed and sorrowful of heart.
sentences.n: بين يديه, 'between his two hands', is the idiom for 'in front of him, in his presence'. باكية العين حزينة القلب are two adjectives each followed by a noun in the genitive ('weeping of eye, sad of heart'); the two phrases also chime in rhythm.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ يَا قُوتَ الْقُلُوبِ أَرَاكِ تَتَظَلَّمِينَ مِنِّي وَتَنْسِبِينَنِي إِلَى الظُّلْمِ وَتَزْعُمِينَ أَنِّي أَسَأْتُ لِمَنْ أَحْسَنَ إِلَيَّ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla yā Qūta al-Qulūbi arāki tataẓallamīna minnī wa-tansibīnanī ilā al-ẓulmi wa-tazʿumīna annī asaʾtu li-man aḥsana ilayya
sentences.l: So-he-said: O Qūt al-Qulūb, I-see-you complaining-of-wrong from-me, and-ascribing-me to the-wrong-doing, and-claiming that-I did-ill to-whoever did-good to-me.
sentences.i: Then he said: O Qūt al-Qulūb, I see you complaining of wrong at my hands, charging me with injustice, and claiming that I have done ill to one who did good to me.
sentences.n: تتظلمين مني: taẓallama min- is 'to complain of wrong done by someone'. أسأت لمن, 'I did ill to whom', uses لـ where Classical Arabic would often say إلى; both occur. The printed form is أسأت with the edition's own precomposed hamza.

sentences.t: فَمَنْ هُوَ الَّذِي حَفِظَ حُرْمَتِي وَأْنَتَهَكْتُ حُرْمَتَهُ وَسَتَرَ حَرِيمِي وَسَبَيْتُ حَرِيمَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-man huwa al-ladhī ḥafiẓa ḥurmatī wa-intahaktu ḥurmatahu wa-satara ḥarīmī wa-sabaytu ḥarīmahu
sentences.l: So-who is he, the-one-who guarded my-inviolability and-I-violated his-inviolability, and-screened my-harem and-I-took-captive his-harem?
sentences.i: Who, then, is the one who guarded my honour while I violated his, who screened my harem while I carried off his women as captives?
sentences.n: The verbs وانتهكت and وسبيت are first person, 'I violated', 'I took captive'; the sentence is the Caliph's own admission, and the second clause of each pair is circumstantial ('while I ...'). حرمة is what is sacred or inviolable about a person; حريم is the women of the household, the harem.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ هُوَ غَانِمُ بْنُ أَيُّوبَ فَإِنَّهُ لَمْ يَقْرَبْنِي بِفَاحِشَةٍ وَلَا سُوءٍ وَحَقِّ نِعْمَتِكَ يَا أَمِيرَالْمُؤْمِنِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu huwa Ghānimu bnu Ayyūba fa-innahu lam yaqrabnī bi-fāḥishatin wa-lā sūʾin wa-ḥaqqi niʿmatika yā amīra al-muʾminīna
sentences.l: So-she-said to-him: He is Ghānim son-of Ayyūb, for-he did-not approach-me with-an-indecency nor evil, and-by-the-right-of your-bounty, O Commander-of the-believers.
sentences.i: She said to him: He is Ghānim ibn Ayyūb; for he never came near me with any indecency or ill, by the right of your bounty, O Commander of the Faithful.
sentences.n: يقربني بفاحشة: qaraba bi- is 'to approach with (an act)', and فاحشة is any gross indecency, here sexual. The slave girl swears that Ghānim never touched her. أميرالمؤمنين is printed as one word.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْخَلِيفَةُ لَاحَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّابِاللَّهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-khalīfatu lā ḥawla wa-lā quwwata illā bi-allāhi
sentences.l: So-said the-caliph: There-is-no power and-no strength except through-God.
sentences.i: The Caliph said: There is no power and no strength save in God.
sentences.n: لاحول and الابالله are each printed as a single word. The formula is a common cry of dismay or resignation.

sentences.t: يَا قُوتَ الْقُلُوبِ تَمَنَّيْ عَلَيَّ تُعْطَىْ
sentences.tr: yā Qūta al-Qulūbi tamannay ʿalayya tuʿṭay
sentences.l: O Qūt al-Qulūb, wish upon-me, you-will-be-given.
sentences.i: O Qūt al-Qulūb, ask a wish of me and it shall be granted you.
sentences.n: تمني is the feminine imperative, 'wish!'. The printed تعطى is the passive of أعطى; the damma on the first letter is the edition's own and is kept. The apodosis (the result clause) has no fa- or particle: 'ask, you will be given'. A fully Classical feminine form would end -ayna or, as jussive after an imperative, -ay; the sukūn on the final yā is ours.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ أَتَمَنَّى عَلَيْكَ مَحْبُوبِي غَانِمَ بْنَ أَيُّوبَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat atamannā ʿalayka maḥbūbī Ghānima bna Ayyūba
sentences.l: So-she-said: I-wish upon-you my-beloved, Ghānim son-of Ayyūb.
sentences.i: She said: The wish I ask of you is my beloved, Ghānim ibn Ayyūb.
sentences.n: Here تمنّى takes its wish as a direct object, so غانم is in the accusative: 'I wish upon you (for) my beloved'.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ امْتَثَلَ أَمْرَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika imtathala amrahā
sentences.l: So-at that, he-complied-with her-command.
sentences.i: At that he complied with her request.
sentences.n: The subject of امتثل is the Caliph. امتثل أمره, 'he carried out his order', is usually said of a subordinate obeying; here the Caliph defers to her.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ يَا أَمِيرَالْمُؤْمِنِينَ إِنْ أَحْضَرْتَهُ تَهَبُنِي لَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat yā amīra al-muʾminīna in aḥḍartahu tahabunī lahu
sentences.l: So-she-said: O Commander-of the-believers, if you-brought-him, you-give-me to-him.
sentences.i: She said: O Commander of the Faithful, if you bring him here, will you give me to him?
sentences.n: Printed تهبني is read as the indicative تهبُني. In Classical Arabic the result clause after إن with a past-tense condition would be jussive or begin with فـ; the bare indicative is a Middle Arabic habit, and the sense here is almost a question or request. Compare the next line, where the Caliph answers with the perfect وهبتك.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ إِنْ حَضَرَ وَهَبْتُكِ لَهُ هِبَةَ كَرِيمٍ لَايَرُدُّ فِي عَطَائِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla in ḥaḍara wahabtuki lahu hibata karīmin lā yaruddu fī ʿaṭāʾihi
sentences.l: So-he-said: If he-comes, I-have-given-you to-him, a-gift-of a-generous-man who-does-not take-back in-his-giving.
sentences.i: He said: If he comes, I give you to him, with the gift of a generous man who takes nothing back from what he has given.
sentences.n: وهبتك is a perfect used for a promise ('I hereby give you'), as in Classical legal and promissory speech. هبة كريم is an adverbial accusative (cognate), 'a gift such as a generous man gives'. لايرد is printed as one word.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ يَاأَمِيرَالْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَذِنْ لِي أَنْ أَدُورَ عَلَيْهِ لَعَلَّ اللَّهَ يَجْمَعُنِي بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat yā amīra al-muʾminīna adhin lī an adūra ʿalayhi laʿalla allāha yajmaʿunī bihi
sentences.l: So-she-said: O Commander-of-the-believers, permit to-me that I-go-round for-him, perhaps God will-gather-me with-him.
sentences.i: She said: O Commander of the Faithful, allow me to go about searching for him; perhaps God will bring us together.
sentences.n: أذن is printed with the precomposed hamza and is read as the imperative of أَذِنَ 'to permit' (Classical اِئْذَنْ). دار على is 'to go round in search of'. يجمعني به, 'will gather me with him', is the idiom for being reunited. يااميرالمؤمنين is printed as one word.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا إِفْعَلِي مَابَدَالَكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā ifʿalī mā badā laki
sentences.l: So-he-said to-her: Do what appears to-you.
sentences.i: He said to her: Do whatever seems good to you.
sentences.n: مابدالك is printed as one word, ما بدا لك, 'whatever appears (good) to you'.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَتْ وَخَرَجَتْ وَمَعَهَا أَلْفُ دِينَارٍ ذَهَبٍ فَزَارَتِ الْمَشَائِخَ وَتَصَدَّقَتْ عَنْهُ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥat wa-kharajat wa-maʿahā alfu dīnārin dhahabin fa-zārati al-mashāʾikha wa-taṣaddaqat ʿanhu
sentences.l: And-she-rejoiced and-went-out, and-with-her a-thousand dinars of-gold; and-she-visited the-elders and-gave-alms on-his-behalf.
sentences.i: She rejoiced and went out, with a thousand dinars of gold in her keeping, and she visited the elders and gave alms for his sake.
sentences.n: المشائخ is the printed Middle Arabic plural for classical مشايخ (mashāyikh), 'elders, sheikhs'. Here the sense is holy men or notables to whom alms are given. The 'his' in عنه is Ghānim, the absent beloved: she gives in his name.

sentences.t: وَطَلَعَتْ ثَانِيَ يَوْمٍ إِلَى سُوقِ التُّجَّارِ وَأَعْلَمَتْ شَيْخَ السُّوقِ
sentences.tr: wa-ṭalaʿat thāniya yawmin ilā sūqi al-tujjāri wa-aʿlamat shaykha al-sūqi
sentences.l: And-she-went-up second-of day to the-market of-the-merchants, and-informed the-sheikh of-the-market.
sentences.i: The next day she went up to the merchants' market and sent word to the master of the market.
sentences.n: ثاني يوم, literally 'second day', is a colloquial way of saying 'the next day'. طلع, 'went up', is the common Middle Arabic verb for 'go out, go up (to the market)'. أعلمت here means that she sent for or notified him; the sheikh of the market is the ʿarīf, the officer in charge of the guild or bazaar (see below).

sentences.t: وَأَعْطَتْ لَهُ دَرَاهِمَ وَقَالَتْ لَهُ تَصَدَّقْ بِهَا عَلَى الْغُرَبَاءِ
sentences.tr: wa-aʿṭat lahu darāhima wa-qālat lahu taṣaddaq bi-hā ʿalā al-ghurabāʾi
sentences.l: And-she-gave to-him dirhams, and-said to-him: Give-alms with-them upon the-strangers.
sentences.i: She gave him some dirhams and said to him: Give these in alms to the strangers.
sentences.n: أعطت له, 'she gave to him', puts the recipient behind لـ, where Classical would take him directly. Expect this often.

sentences.t: وَطَلَعَتْ
sentences.tr: wa-ṭalaʿat
sentences.l: And-she-went-up.
sentences.i: And she went up.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ جَاءَتْ ثَانِيَ جُمْعَةٍ السُّوقَ وَمَعَهَا أَلْفُ دِينَارٍ وَدَخَلَتْ سُوقَ الصَّاغَةِ وَسُوقَ الْجَوْهَرِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: thumma jāʾat thāniya jumʿatin al-sūqa wa-maʿahā alfu dīnārin wa-dakhalat sūqa al-ṣāghati wa-sūqa al-jawharīyati
sentences.l: Then she-came second-of week the-market, and-with-her a-thousand dinars, and-she-entered the-market of-the-goldsmiths and-the-market of-the-jewellers.
sentences.i: The week after, she came again to the market with a thousand dinars, and entered the goldsmiths' market and the jewellers' market.
sentences.n: ثاني جمعة is read here as 'the second week, the following week' (جمعة can mean 'week' as well as Friday in later Arabic); the printed text has no preposition before السوق, so it is taken as the place she came to. The reading is mine; 'the second Friday' is the other possibility.

sentences.t: فَنَادَتْ بِالْعَرِيفِ فَحَضَرَ فَدَفَعَتْ لَهُ أَلْفَ دِينَارٍ وَقَانَتْ لَهُ تَصَدَّقْ بِهَا عَلَى الْغُرَبَاءِ
sentences.tr: fa-nādat bi-al-ʿarīfi fa-ḥaḍara fa-dafaʿat lahu alfa dīnārin wa-qānat lahu taṣaddaq bi-hā ʿalā al-ghurabāʾi
sentences.l: And-she-called for-the-overseer, and-he-came; and-she-handed to-him a-thousand dinars, and-said(?) to-him: Give-alms with-them upon the-strangers.
sentences.i: She called for the overseer, and he came; and she handed him a thousand dinars and said to him: Give these in alms to the strangers.
sentences.n: وقانت is the printed form; the sense and the parallel sentence above show that وقالت, 'and she said', is meant (ن for ل). I point what is printed and read it as a slip. العريف is the overseer or headman of a market or quarter.

sentences.t: فَنَظَرَ إِلَيْهَا الْعَرِيفُ وَهُوَ شَيْخُ السُّوقِ وَقَالَ لَهَا يَاسِتِّي هَلْ لَكِ أَنْ تَذْهَبِي إِلَى دَارِي وَتَنْظُرِي إِلَى هَذَا الشَّابِّ الْغَرِيبِ مَا أَظْرَفَهُ وَمَا أَكْمَلَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-naẓara ilayhā al-ʿarīfu wa-huwa shaykhu al-sūqi wa-qāla lahā yā sittī hal laki an tadhhabī ilā dārī wa-tanẓurī ilā hādhā al-shābbi al-gharībi mā aẓrafahu wa-mā akmalahu
sentences.l: And-he-looked at-her, the-overseer, and-he the-sheikh of-the-market, and-said to-her: O-my-lady, is-there for-you that you-go to my-house and-look at this youth, the-stranger, how-charming-he! and-how-perfect-he!
sentences.i: The overseer, who was the master of the market, looked at her and said: My lady, will you come to my house and look at this young stranger? How graceful he is, and how perfect!
sentences.n: ياستي is printed as one word: yā sittī, 'my lady', ست being the colloquial form of سيدة. هل لك أن … is 'would you care to …', literally 'is there for you that …'. ما أظرفه is the exclamatory 'how charming he is!'. The word-order in this sentence follows the print.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ هُوَ غَانِمَ بْنَ أَيُّوبَ الْمُتَيَّمَ الْمَسْلُوبَ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna huwa Ghānima ibna Ayyūba al-mutayyama al-maslūba
sentences.l: And-was he Ghānim son-of Ayyūb, the-love-enslaved, the-despoiled.
sentences.i: And this young man was none other than Ghānim ibn Ayyūb, the love-struck and despoiled.
sentences.n: A narrator's aside: the overseer does not know who he is. المتيم (mutayyam) is one whom love has enslaved; المسلوب is one who has been stripped of his goods.

sentences.t: وَلَكِنَّ الْعَرِيفَ لَيْسَ لَهُ بِهِ مَعْرِفَةٌ وَكَانَ يَظُنُّ أَنَّهُ رَجُلٌ مِسْكِينٌ مَدْيُونٌ سُلِبَتْ نِعْمَتُهُ أَوْعَاشِقٌ فَارَقَ أَحِبَّتَهُ
sentences.tr: wa-lākinna al-ʿarīfa laysa lahu bihi maʿrifatun wa-kāna yaẓunnu annahu rajulun miskīnun madyūnun sulibat niʿmatuhu aw ʿāshiqun fāraqa aḥibbatahu
sentences.l: But the-overseer, not for-him with-him acquaintance, and-he-was thinking that-he a-man poor, indebted, was-taken-away his-prosperity, or a-lover, he-parted-from his-beloved-ones.
sentences.i: But the overseer had no knowledge of him, and supposed him to be some poor man in debt whose fortune had been taken from him, or a lover parted from those he loved.
sentences.n: The print has ولكن without the doubled nūn; I point it as وَلَكِنَّ, which governs العريف. 'Sulibat niʿmatuhu', 'his prosperity was taken away', is a relative clause on مديون without a linking word, as often in Middle Arabic. أحبته is the plural of حبيب, 'beloved ones'.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ كَلَامَهُ خَفَقَ قَلْبُهَا وَتَقَلْقَلَتْ أَحْشَاؤُهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat kalāmahu khafaqa qalbuhā wa-taqalqalat aḥshāʾuhā
sentences.l: And-when she-heard his-speech, throbbed her-heart, and-were-shaken her-innards.
sentences.i: When she heard his words, her heart pounded and her very bowels were shaken.
sentences.n: She hears of a stranger in distress and suspects it is Ghānim. أحشاء, 'entrails, innards', is the seat of deep feeling in Arabic, as 'heart' is in English; I keep the physical word.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ أَسِلْ مَعِي مَنْ يُوصِلُنِي إِلَى دَارِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu asil maʿī man yūṣilunī ilā dārika
sentences.l: And-she-said to-him: (Send) with-me one-who will-bring-me to your-house.
sentences.i: Then she said to him: Send someone with me to bring me to your house.
sentences.n: اسل is printed; it can only be a slip for ارسل (arsil), 'send', with the ر dropped, since the next sentence has فأرسل. I point it as printed, أَسِلْ, and translate 'send'.

sentences.t: فَأَرْسَلَ مَعَهَا صَبِيًّا صَغِيرًا فَأَوْصَلَهَا إِلَى الدَّارِ الَّتِي فِيهَا الْغَرِيبُ لِلْعَرِيفِ
sentences.tr: fa-arsala maʿahā ṣabīyan ṣaghīran fa-awṣalahā ilā al-dāri allatī fīhā al-gharību li-al-ʿarīfi
sentences.l: So-he-sent with-her a-boy, small, and-he-brought-her to the-house which in-it the-stranger, belonging-to-the-overseer.
sentences.i: So he sent a small boy with her, and the boy brought her to the house where the stranger was, the overseer's own house.
sentences.n: للعريف: li- of possession, 'belonging to the overseer', added after the relative clause; it makes explicit that this is the house he had offered.

sentences.t: فَشَكَرَتْهُ عَلَى ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-shakarathu ʿalā dhālika
sentences.l: And-she-thanked-him for that.
sentences.i: So she thanked him for that.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا وَصَلَتِ الْبَيْتَ وَدَخَلَتْ وَسَلَّمَتْ عَلَى زَوْجَةِ الْعَرِيفِ قَامَتْ زَوْجَةُ الْعَرِيفِ فَقَبَّلَتِ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهَا لِأَنَّهَا عَرَفَتْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā waṣalat al-bayta wa-dakhalat wa-sallamat ʿalā zawjati al-ʿarīfi qāmat zawjatu al-ʿarīfi fa-qabbalat al-arḍa bayna yadayhā li-annahā ʿarafathā
sentences.l: And-when she-reached the-house and-entered and-greeted the-wife-of the-overseer, the-wife-of the-overseer rose and-kissed the-ground between her-two-hands, because-she had-known-her.
sentences.i: When she reached the house, went in, and gave greeting to the overseer's wife, the overseer's wife rose and kissed the ground before her, for she knew who she was.
sentences.n: العريف is the overseer, the headman of the market or quarter, the man who knows the people of his quarter. بين يديها, 'between her two hands', means 'in front of her', the posture of a subject before a superior. The wife kisses the ground out of respect, because she recognises Qūt al-Qulūb as the great lady, the Caliph's favourite.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهَا قُوتُ الْقُلُوبِ أَيْنَ الضَّعِيفُ الَّذِي عِنْدَكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahā Qūtu al-Qulūbi ayna al-ḍaʿīfu al-ladhī ʿindaki
sentences.l: And-she-said to-her, Qūt al-Qulūb: Where the-weak-one who at-you?
sentences.i: Then Qūt al-Qulūb said to her: Where is the sick man who is with you?
sentences.n: الضعيف, 'the weak one', here a man in a state of weakness and want: the sick stranger lodged in the sergeant's house.

sentences.t: فَبَكَتْ وَقَالَتْ هَاهُوَ يَاسِتِّي وَاللَّهِ إِنَّهُ ابْنُ نَاسٍ وَعَلَيْهِ أَثَرُ النِّعْمَةِ وَذَلِكَ هُوَ عَلَى الْفِرَاشِ
sentences.tr: fa-bakat wa-qālat hā-huwa yā sittī wa-Allāhi innahu ibnu nāsin wa-ʿalayhi atharu al-niʿmati wa-dhālika huwa ʿalā al-firāshi
sentences.l: And-she-wept and-said: Here-he, O my-lady! By-God, indeed-he a-son-of people, and-upon-him a-mark-of the-bounty; and-that-one he upon the-bed.
sentences.i: The woman wept and said: Here he is, my lady. By God, he is a man of good family, and the marks of former plenty are on him. That is he, there on the bed.
sentences.n: ابن ناس, 'son of people', means a person of good birth and standing. ياستي is yā sitt-ī, 'O my lady', printed as one word with the ست spelled with a single ت; the shadda is supplied.

sentences.t: فَالْتَفَتَتْ إِلَيْهِ وَنَظَرَتْهُ فَرَأَتْهُ كَأَنَّهُ هُوَ بِذَاتِهِ وَرَأَتْهُ قَدِ اخْتَفَى وَكَثُرَ نُحُولُهُ وَرَقَّ إِلَى أَنْ صَارَ كَالْخِلَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-iltafatat ilayhi wa-naẓarathu fa-raʾathu ka-annahu huwa bi-dhātihi wa-raʾathu qadi ikhtafā wa-kathura nuḥūluhu wa-raqqa ilā an ṣāra ka-al-khilāli
sentences.l: And-she-turned to-him and-looked-at-him, and-saw-him as-though-he he in-his-very-self, and-saw-him had vanished and-abounded his-wasting and-grew-thin until he-became like-the-toothpick.
sentences.i: She turned to him and looked at him, and she saw one who might be he himself; yet she saw too that he had faded away, that his wasting had grown great, and that he had thinned until he was like a toothpick.
sentences.n: اختفى, 'he disappeared', is used here of a man who has all but vanished: wasted away. الخلال is the toothpick (khilāl), a figure for extreme thinness. Note that she sees 'as though it is he' but cannot be sure: the next sentence says so.

sentences.t: وَانْبَهَمَ عَلَيْهَا أَمْرُهُ فَلَمْ تَتَحَقَّقْ أَنَّهُ هُوَ
sentences.tr: wa-inbahama ʿalayhā amruhu fa-lam tataḥaqqaq annahu huwa
sentences.l: And-became-obscure upon-her his-affair, and-she-did-not make-certain that-he he.
sentences.i: But his case was dark to her, and she could not be sure that it was he.
sentences.n: انبهم, 'became obscure, indistinct', is the VII-form of أبهم; the thing is blurred to her, so she cannot confirm his identity.

sentences.t: وَلَكِنْ أَخَذَتْهَا الشَّفَقَةُ عَلَيْهِ فَبَكَتْ وَقَالَتْ إِنَّ الْغُرَبَاءَ مَسَاكِينُ وَإِنْ كَانُوا أُمَرَاءَ فِي بِلَادِهِمْ
sentences.tr: wa-lākin akhadhathā al-shafaqatu ʿalayhi fa-bakat wa-qālat inna al-ghurabāʾa masākīnu wa-in kānū umarāʾa fī bilādihim
sentences.l: But took-her the-pity upon-him, and-she-wept and-said: Indeed the-strangers poor-ones, even-if they-were princes in their-lands.
sentences.i: Yet pity took hold of her for him, and she wept and said: Strangers are wretched folk, even though they were princes in their own lands.

sentences.t: وَقَدْتَعَنَّتَ عَلَيْهَا وَلَمْ تَعْرِفْ أَنَّهُ غَانِمٌ
sentences.tr: wa-qad taʿannata ʿalayhā wa-lam taʿrif annahu Ghānimun
sentences.l: And-already-it-was-hard upon-her, and-she-did-not know that-he Ghānim.
sentences.i: It weighed hard upon her, and she did not know that he was Ghānim.
sentences.n: وقدتعنّت is printed as one word, with the shadda on the ن. I read the verb as taʿannata, 'it was hard, troublesome' to her, with the matter as understood subject; with one final ت it is masculine, and a feminine verb would need two. Both the sense and the form are uncertain, and the word may be a slip.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا وَجَعَهَا قَلْبُهَا عَلَيْهِ وَرَتَّبَتْ لَهُ الشَّرَابَ وَالْأَدْوِيَةَ
sentences.tr: thumma innahā wajaʿahā qalbuhā ʿalayhi wa-rattabat lahu al-sharāba wa-al-adwiyata
sentences.l: Then indeed-she, ached-her her-heart over-him, and-she-arranged for-him the-drink and-the-medicines.
sentences.i: Then her heart ached for him, and she set in order for him his draughts and medicines.
sentences.n: وجعها قلبها: wajaʿa is used transitively, 'her heart pained her', a construction found in the later colloquial-leaning style of the text, not in strict Classical (which would say وَجِعَ قَلْبُهَا).

sentences.t: ثُمَّ جَلَسَتْ عِنْدَ رَأْسِهِ سَاعَةً
sentences.tr: thumma jalasat ʿinda raʾsihi sāʿatan
sentences.l: Then she-sat at his-head an-hour.
sentences.i: Then she sat at his head for an hour.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ رَكِبَتْ وَطَلَعَتْ إِلَى قَصْرِهَا وَصَارَتْ تَطْلَعُ كُلَّ سُوقٍ لِأَجْلِ التَّفْتِيشِ عَلَى غَانِمٍ
sentences.tr: thumma rakibat wa-ṭalaʿat ilā qaṣrihā wa-ṣārat taṭlaʿu kulla sūqin li-ajli al-taftīshi ʿalā Ghānimin
sentences.l: Then she-rode and-went-up to her-palace, and-became going-up every market for-the-sake-of the-searching for Ghānim.
sentences.i: Then she mounted and went up to her palace, and she took to going through every market, for the sake of searching for Ghānim.
sentences.n: طلعت إلى قصرها: ṭalaʿa is 'go up, go out', used loosely for going to the palace. تطلع كل سوق is 'she goes up every market', that is, she goes out to every market in turn.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْعَرِيفَ قَدْأَتَى بِأُمِّهِ وَأُخْتِهِ فِتْنَةَ وَدَخَلَ بِهِمَا عَلَى قُوتِ الْقُلُوبِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-ʿarīfa qad atā bi-ummihi wa-ukhtihi Fitnata wa-dakhala bihimā ʿalā Qūti al-Qulūbi
sentences.l: Then indeed the-overseer had-come with-his-mother and-his-sister Fitna, and-entered with-the-two-of-them upon Qūt al-Qulūb.
sentences.i: Then the overseer came, bringing Ghānim's mother and his sister Fitna, and led them in to Qūt al-Qulūb.
sentences.n: قداتى is printed as one word, qad + atā. The “his” of “his mother and his sister” is Ghānim, not yet named in this sentence. The العريف is the overseer or headman of a quarter or guild.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ يَا سَيِّدَةَ الْمُحْسِنَاتِ قَدْ دَخَلَ مَدِينَتَنَا فِي هَذَا الْيَوْمِ إِمْرَأَةٌ وَبِنْتُهَا
sentences.tr: wa-qāla yā sayyidata al-muḥsināti qad dakhala madīnatanā fī hādhā al-yawmi imraʾatun wa-bintuhā
sentences.l: And-he-said: O lady-of the-doers-of-good (f. pl.), has-entered our-city in this the-day a-woman and-her-daughter.
sentences.i: And he said: O mistress of the women who do good, a woman and her daughter came into our city today.
sentences.n: Middle Arabic and ordinary Arabic both let dakhala take its place directly, without a preposition: “entered our city”.

sentences.t: وَهُمَا وُجُوهٌ مِلَاحٌ وَعَلَيْهِمَا أَثَرُ النِّعْمَةِ وَالسَّعَادَةِ عَلَيْهِمَا لَائِحَةٌ
sentences.tr: wa-humā wujūhun milāḥun wa-ʿalayhimā athru al-niʿmati wa-al-saʿādati ʿalayhimā lāʾiḥatun
sentences.l: And-they-two faces fair, and-upon-the-two-of-them trace-of the-ease and-the-felicity, upon-the-two-of-them showing (f.).
sentences.i: They are fair of face, and the marks of ease and happiness still show plainly upon them,
sentences.n: وجوه ملاح, “faces fair”, gives a plural predicate to a dual subject: the sense is simply “they have comely faces”. لائحة is feminine and agrees loosely with السعادة rather than with the masculine أثر.

sentences.t: لَكِنَّهُمَا لَابِسَتَانِ ثِيَابًا مِنَ الشَّعَرِ
sentences.tr: lākinnahumā lābisatāni thiyāban mina al-shaʿari
sentences.l: but-the-two-of-them wearing-(f. dual) garments of the-hair.
sentences.i: yet they are clad in garments of hair-cloth.
sentences.n: الشعر is read here as shaʿar, hair, the coarse goat-hair stuff of penitents and beggars (not shiʿr, poetry).

sentences.t: وَكُلُّ وَاحِدَةٍ مِنْهُمَا مُعَلِّقَةٌ فِي رَقَبَتِهَا مِخْلَاةٌ
sentences.tr: wa-kullu wāḥidatin minhumā muʿallaqatun fī raqabatihā mikhlātun
sentences.l: And-each one of-the-two-of-them hung in her-neck a-wallet.
sentences.i: and each of them has a wallet hung about her neck,
sentences.n: مخلاة is a bag of cloth, properly a nose-bag for fodder, here the beggar's wallet for collected scraps.

sentences.t: وَعُيُونُهُمَا بَاكِيَةٌ وَقُلُوبُهُمَا حَزِينَةٌ
sentences.tr: wa-ʿuyūnuhumā bākiyatun wa-qulūbuhumā ḥazīnatun
sentences.l: and-their-eyes weeping, and-their-hearts sorrowful.
sentences.i: their eyes weeping and their hearts sorrowful.

sentences.t: وَهَا أَنَا أَتَيْتُ بِهِمَا إِلَيْكِ لِتَأْوِيهِمَا وَتَصُونِيهِمَا عَنِ الشَّحَاذَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-hā anā ataytu bihimā ilayki li-taʾwīhimā wa-taṣūnīhimā ʿani al-shaḥādhati
sentences.l: And-behold I, I-came with-the-two-of-them to-you (f.), so-that-you-shelter-them and-you-guard-them from the-begging.
sentences.i: And here I am, I have brought them to you, that you may give them shelter and keep them from begging.
sentences.n: The ي in لتأويهما and وتصونيهما is the ending of the feminine “you” (the subjunctive of a verb addressed to a woman), followed by the pronoun “them”. So the overseer is speaking to Qūt al-Qulūb. The print has تأوي with plain hamza-on-alif, which points to ʾawā (form I, “give shelter to”) rather than ʾāwā (form IV, normally written تؤوي); both exist and mean the same.

sentences.t: لِأَنَّهُمَا لَيْسَتَا أَهْلًا لِلشَّحَاذَةِ
sentences.tr: li-annahumā laysatā ahlan li-al-shaḥādhati
sentences.l: because-the-two-of-them not-are-(f. dual) worthy for-the-begging.
sentences.i: for they are not fit to beg.

sentences.t: وَإِنَّنَا نَدْخُلُ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ بِهِمَا الْجَنَّةَ
sentences.tr: wa-innanā nadkhulu in shāʾa Allāhu bihimā al-jannata
sentences.l: And-indeed-we we-enter, if willed God, with-the-two-of-them the-garden (Paradise).
sentences.i: and through them, God willing, we shall enter Paradise.
sentences.n: نَدْخُلُ بِهِمَا الْجَنَّةَ, “we enter Paradise by means of them”: the بـ here is of means, and the verb takes Paradise directly.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ وَاللَّهِ يَاسَيِّدِي لَقَدْ شَوَّقْتَنِي إِلَيْهِمَا وَأَيْنَ هُمَا
sentences.tr: fa-qālat wa-Allāhi yā sayyidī la-qad shawwaqtanī ilayhimā wa-ayna humā
sentences.l: And-she-said: By-God, O-my-master, indeed you-made-yearn me for-the-two-of-them; and-where the-two-of-them?
sentences.i: She said: By God, my lord, you have made me long to see them! Where are they?
sentences.n: يَاسَيِّدِي is printed as one word, yā sayyidī. She is addressing the overseer.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لِلْعَرِيفِ عَلَيَّ بِهِمَا فَأَمَرَ الْخَادِمَ أَنْ يُدْخِلَهُمَا عَلَى قُوتِ الْقُلُوبِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat li-al-ʿarīfi ʿalayya bihimā fa-amara al-khādima an yudkhilahumā ʿalā Qūti al-Qulūbi
sentences.l: And-she-said to-the-overseer: Upon-me with-the-two-of-them! And-he-ordered the-servant that he-bring-in-them upon Qūt al-Qulūb.
sentences.i: Then she said to the overseer: Bring them to me! And he commanded the servant to show them in to Qūt al-Qulūb.
sentences.n: عليّ بهما is a clipped command: “(let it be) upon me, (the bringing of) them”, that is, “bring them to me”. The printed shadda on عليّ is the edition's own and is kept. The verb أمر is masculine, so it is the overseer who gives the order; the servant (a eunuch) is the household's attendant.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ دَخَلَتْ فِتْنَةُ وَأُمُّهَا عَلَى قُوتِ الْقُلُوبِ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika dakhalat Fitnatu wa-ummuhā ʿalā Qūti al-Qulūbi
sentences.l: And-at that entered Fitna and-her-mother upon Qūt al-Qulūb.
sentences.i: Thereupon Fitna and her mother went in to Qūt al-Qulūb.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا نَظَرَتْهُمَا قُوتُ الْقُلُوبِ وَهُمَا ذَاتَا جَمَالٍ بَكَتْ عَلَيْهِمَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā naẓarathumā Qūtu al-Qulūbi wa-humā dhātā jamālin bakat ʿalayhimā
sentences.l: And-when looked-at-the-two-of-them Qūt al-Qulūb, and-they-two possessors-(f. dual)-of beauty, she-wept over-the-two-of-them.
sentences.i: When Qūt al-Qulūb looked on them and saw how beautiful they were, she wept for them,

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ وَاللَّهِ إِنَّهُمَا أَوْلَادُ نِعْمَةٍ وَيَلُوحُ عَلَيْهِمَا أَثَرُ الْغِنَى
sentences.tr: wa-qālat wa-Allāhi innahumā awlādu niʿmatin wa-yalūḥu ʿalayhimā athru al-ghinā
sentences.l: and-she-said: By-God, indeed-the-two-of-them children-of ease, and-shows upon-the-two-of-them trace-of the-wealth.
sentences.i: and said: By God, these two are children of comfort, and the mark of wealth shows upon them.
sentences.n: أولاد is the plural of walad, “child”, used loosely for a daughter and a mother: “people raised in ease”.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ زَوْجَةُ الْعَرِيفِ يَاسِتِّي نَحْنُ نُحِبُّ الْفُقَرَاءَ وَالْمَسَاكِينَ لِأَجْلِ الثَّوَابِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat zawjatu al-ʿarīfi yā sittī naḥnu nuḥibbu al-fuqarāʾa wa-al-masākīna li-ajli al-thawābi
sentences.l: And-said the-wife-of the-overseer: O-my-lady, we, we-love the-poor and-the-needy for-the-sake-of the-reward.
sentences.i: Then the overseer's wife said: My lady, we love the poor and the needy, for the sake of the reward.
sentences.n: يَاسِتِّي is printed as one word, yā sittī, “my lady”. الثواب is the reward that God gives for good deeds.

sentences.t: وَهَؤُلَاءِ رُبَّمَا جَارُوا عَلَيْهِمَا الظَّلَمَةُ وَسَلَبُوا نِعْمَتَهُمَا وَأَخْرَبُوا دِيَارَهُمَا
sentences.tr: wa-hāʾulāʾi rubbamā jārū ʿalayhimā al-ẓalamatu wa-salabū niʿmatahumā wa-akhrabū diyārahumā
sentences.l: And-these perhaps wronged upon-the-two-of-them the-oppressors, and-despoiled their-two-favour, and-laid-waste their-two-homes.
sentences.i: As for these two, perhaps the oppressors wronged them, stripped them of their comfort, and laid their homes in ruins.
sentences.n: Two Middle Arabic habits: the plural هؤلاء is used of two women, and the plural verb جاروا comes before its subject الظلمة (classically it would be jāra). Both are common in this register.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمَا بَكَتَابُكَاءً شَدِيدًا وَافْتَكَرَتَا مِمَّا كَانَتَا فِيهِ مِنَ النِّعَمِ وَمَا بَقَتَافِيهِ مِنَ الْفَقْرِ وَالْحُزْنِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahumā bakatā bukāʾan shadīdan wa-iftakaratā mimmā kānatā fīhi mina al-niʿami wa-mā baqatā fīhi mina al-faqri wa-al-ḥuzni
sentences.l: Then indeed-the-two-of-them wept-(dual) weeping intense, and-recalled-(dual) of-what they-were-(dual) in-it of the-favours, and-what they-became-(dual) in-it of the-poverty and-the-grief.
sentences.i: Then the two of them wept bitterly, and called to mind the blessings they had once lived in, and the poverty and grief to which they had come.
sentences.n: بكتابكاء is printed as one word: bakatā + bukāʾan. بقتافيه is likewise baqatā + fīhi. The print has بقتا with no yāʾ; I read it as the colloquial baqat, “became”, which is how Egyptian Arabic uses baqā (classical baqiyat would be “remained”). Either way the sense is “what they had come to be in”.

sentences.t: وَتَفَكَّرَتَا غَانِمَ بْنَ أَيُّوبَ الْمُتَيَّمَ الْمَسْلُوبَ
sentences.tr: wa-tafakkaratā Ghānima ibna Ayyūba al-mutayyama al-maslūba
sentences.l: And-pondered-(dual) Ghānim son-of Ayyūb, the-love-enslaved, the-despoiled.
sentences.i: And they thought of Ghānim son of Ayyūb, the love-struck, the despoiled.
sentences.n: The verb takes Ghānim as a direct object: “they brooded on Ghānim”. المتيم is one whom love has enslaved and unmanned; المسلوب is one who has been stripped of his goods.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا بَكَتَا بَكَتْ قُوتُ الْقُلُوبِ لِبُكَائِهِمَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā bakatā bakat Qūtu al-Qulūbi li-bukāʾihimā
sentences.l: And-when they-two-wept, wept Qūt al-Qulūb for-their-two-weeping.
sentences.i: When they wept, Qūt al-Qulūb wept to hear their weeping.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتَا نَسْأَلُ اللَّهَ أَنْ يَجْمَعَنَا بِمَنْ نُرِيدُهُ وَهُوَ وَلَدِي اسْمُهُ غَانِمُ ابْنُ أَيُّوبَ
sentences.tr: wa-qālatā nasʾalu Allāha an yajmaʿanā bi-man nurīduhu wa-huwa waladī ismuhu Ghānimu ibnu Ayyūba
sentences.l: And-said-(dual) we-ask God that he-gather us with-whom we-want-him, and-he my-son, his-name Ghānim son-of Ayyūb.
sentences.i: And they said: We ask God to bring us together with the one we long for, who is my son, whose name is Ghānim son of Ayyūb.
sentences.n: The verb is dual (“the two said”), yet the speech slips into the mother's first person singular, “my son”: the mother is the speaker and Fitna joins in. يجمعنا بـ, “gather us with”, takes بـ for the one met.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَتْ قُوتُ الْقُلُوبِ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ عَلِمَتْ أَنَّ هَذِهِ الْمَرْأَةَ أُمُّ مَعْشُوقِهَا وَالْأُخْرَى أَخْتُهُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿat Qūtu al-Qulūbi hādhā al-kalāma ʿalimat anna hādhihi al-marʾata ummu maʿshūqihā wa-al-ukhrā ukhtuhu
sentences.l: And-when heard Qūt al-Qulūb this the-speech, she-knew that this the-woman mother-of her-beloved, and-the-other his-sister.
sentences.i: When Qūt al-Qulūb heard these words, she knew that this woman was the mother of her beloved, and the other his sister.

sentences.t: فَبَكَتْ حَتَّى غُشِيَ عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-bakat ḥattā ghushiya ʿalayhā
sentences.l: And-she-wept until it-was-covered upon-her.
sentences.i: And she wept until she swooned away.
sentences.n: غُشِيَ عَلَيْهَا, literally “it was covered over her”, is the idiom for fainting.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَفَاقَتْ أَقْبَلَتْ عَلَيْهِمَا وَقَالَتْ لَهُمَا لَا بَأْسَ عَلَيْكُمَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā afāqat aqbalat ʿalayhimā wa-qālat lahumā lā baʾsa ʿalaykumā
sentences.l: And-when she-recovered, she-turned upon-the-two-of-them and-said to-the-two-of-them: No harm upon-the-two-of-you.
sentences.i: When she came to herself, she turned to them and said: Have no fear.
sentences.n: لا بأس عليكما, “no harm upon you”, is the stock phrase of reassurance.

sentences.t: وَهَذَا الْيَوْمُ أَوَّلُ سَعَادَتِكُمَا وَآخِرُ شَقَاوَتِكُمَا
sentences.tr: wa-hādhā al-yawmu awwalu saʿādatikumā wa-ākhiru shaqāwatikumā
sentences.l: And-this the-day first-of your-two-felicity and-last-of your-two-wretchedness.
sentences.i: This day is the first of your happiness and the last of your misery.
sentences.n: Note the matching pair أول سعادتكما / آخر شقاوتكما, “first of your bliss / last of your woe”.

sentences.t: فَلَا تَحْزَنَا
sentences.tr: fa-lā taḥzanā
sentences.l: So not grieve-(dual)!
sentences.i: So grieve no more.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُــــــبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And-overtook Shahrazād the-morning, and-she-fell-silent from the-speech the-permitted.
sentences.i: And morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
sentences.n: The closing formula, in rhyme: الصباح / المباح, “the morning / the permitted”. The long stretched mīm-to-bāʾ in المباح is the printer's tatweel (line-filling), kept as printed.
